scope_note: Daily edition from matching Thursday /new listings: 131 non-replacement cs.CV rows, 37 cs.RO rows, 160 deduplicated papers, and 136 ROI papers. Tier A cards use official arXiv abstract pages plus available official arXiv HTML headings.
executive_thesis: The August 6 batch is about deciding which evidence channel is allowed to steer a robot action. CofactVLA treats visual dominance as a causal-confounding problem, Faster-WAM keeps future state available without paying full video-action cost, SAFECAST calibrates failure detectors under contrast-set shifts, and Talk2Sensors moves outdoor grounding toward sensor-specific physical cues. APRL should turn this into an evidence-channel audit: instruction, vision, future state, geometry, and risk probe each need separate perturbations and stop conditions.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: VLA errors are becoming causal evidence errors
decision_cards.body: CofactVLA and GUARD both ask whether the action was grounded in the intended instruction and visual evidence, rather than in a dominant but spurious cue.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Future state must survive the inference budget
decision_cards.body: Faster-WAM, MobileWAM, and DreamWAM separate action-relevant future state from RGB-only prediction and from expensive full future rollout.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Geometry grounding must name the sensor cue
decision_cards.body: Talk2Sensors and the calibration papers make camera, LiDAR, radar, and 3D target cues auditable instead of treating 3D grounding as a single score.

papers.title: CofactVLA: Deconfounding Vision-Language-Action Models via Counterfactual Intervention
papers.fit: VLA causality - vision override - counterfactual intervention
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML structure checked
papers.status_quo: VLA policies often assume the language instruction remains the primary causal driver of action.
papers.friction: Dense visual streams can override sparse language, so policies latch onto familiar layouts or salient objects.
papers.hidden_premise: The model needs a way to compare the instructed action against a language-masked counterfactual branch.
papers.conceptual_move: Formalize VLA action generation as a deconfounding graph and neutralize visual confounders inside one forward pass.
papers.mechanism: The abstract defines vision override as causal confusion and the official HTML exposes causal-view and action-level deconfounding sections.

evidence.claim: The paper names modality imbalance and spurious visual confounders as the cause of instruction bypass.
Official HTML includes a causal view of VLA and action-level deconfounding method sections.
APRL should test whether language ablation changes action choice before accepting a VLA rollout as grounded.

papers.falsification: If counterfactual masking does not separate instruction-sensitive from vision-dominated failures, the causal framing is weak.
papers.adversarial: A masked branch can remove useful context, so gains must be checked under object, layout, and instruction perturbations.
papers.thinking_tool: Before scaling demonstrations, ask which evidence channel would change the next action if removed.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for language-conditioned manipulation; less direct for low-level servo tasks with no linguistic ambiguity.

papers.title: Faster-WAM: Efficient Inference-Time Future Conditioning for Robust World Action Models
papers.fit: world action model - future conditioning - inference efficiency
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML structure checked
papers.status_quo: WAMs often trade future-aware inference for prohibitive video-action computation.
papers.friction: Removing future conditioning saves compute but may discard the temporal state that gives robustness under shift.
papers.hidden_premise: Future representations can be computed once, reused sparsely, and still preserve the action-relevant signal.
papers.conceptual_move: Keep inference-time future conditioning while decoupling it from expensive full video-action interaction.
papers.mechanism: The abstract motivates sparse future conditioning and the official HTML includes problem formulation, method, and experiment sections.

evidence.claim: The paper states that inference-time future conditioning is critical for generalization under distribution shifts.
Official HTML includes Faster-WAM, implementation, and experiment sections.
APRL should measure which future tokens change action success per unit of latency.

papers.falsification: If sparse future conditioning only preserves visual plausibility and not action success under shift, the efficiency gain is insufficient.
papers.adversarial: The method can hide stale-future errors unless the future cache is perturbed and aged in evaluation.
papers.thinking_tool: Treat future state as a budgeted control resource, not as a decorative prediction target.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for WAM-style manipulation and mobile manipulation; less direct for memoryless reactive policies.

papers.title: SAFECAST: Robust Failure Detection for VLA Policies with Contrast-Set Training and Calibration
papers.fit: VLA failure detection - contrast sets - calibrated risk
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML structure checked
papers.status_quo: Hidden-state risk probes are usually calibrated on data that may not match deployment shift.
papers.friction: Clutter, distractors, lighting, novel objects, initial states, and reworded instructions can invalidate calibration.
papers.hidden_premise: A failure detector must see controlled contrastive shifts before deployment, not only nominal successes and failures.
papers.conceptual_move: Use visual and language contrast-set perturbations to train and calibrate VLA failure probes.
papers.mechanism: The abstract reports improved ROC-AUC across DROID and LIBERO, and the official HTML exposes SAFECAST experiments and results sections.

evidence.claim: The paper lists deployment-time shifts and ties detector reliability to matching calibration data.
Official HTML includes experimental setup and failure-detection improvement sections.
APRL should store contrast-set perturbation type next to every failure-warning metric.

papers.falsification: If detector calibration fails on unseen shift families, contrast sets are still too narrow.
papers.adversarial: A high ROC-AUC can hide poor early-warning lead time or poor recovery action quality.
papers.thinking_tool: Calibrate risk probes by the exact shift family that should trigger a different robot decision.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for VLA deployment monitoring; less complete for hardware faults that do not appear in policy hidden state.

papers.title: Talk2Sensors: 3D Visual Grounding in Autonomous Driving via Sensor-Adaptive Physical Cue Matching
papers.fit: outdoor 3D grounding - camera LiDAR radar - physical cue matching
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML structure checked
papers.status_quo: 3D visual grounding is often evaluated indoors or with one dominant outdoor sensing modality.
papers.friction: Outdoor driving queries depend on texture, geometry, and kinematics that different sensors observe unevenly.
papers.hidden_premise: Language grounding should route the query to the physical cue and sensor that can actually verify it.
papers.conceptual_move: Build a camera-LiDAR-4D radar grounding dataset and a sensor-adaptive cue matching framework.
papers.mechanism: The abstract names sensor-specific physical cues, and official HTML includes dataset, annotation, statistics, and method sections.

evidence.claim: The paper reports 8,682 language instructions and 20,558 referred objects aligned with sensor-specific cues.
Official HTML includes camera, LiDAR, radar fusion and dataset statistics sections.
APRL should evaluate 3D grounding by cue-source agreement, not only box accuracy.

papers.falsification: If sensor-adaptive routing fails under weather, range, or occlusion changes, the grounding interface is not robust enough.
papers.adversarial: A dataset can reward sensor-name correlations unless cue-level perturbations are tested.
papers.thinking_tool: For every grounded command, record which sensor cue made the referent observable.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for outdoor autonomy and multi-sensor robots; less direct for single-camera tabletop manipulation.

synthesis.title: Evidence channels replace monolithic policy confidence
synthesis.facts: The papers separate instruction causality, hidden-state risk, and token/KV grounding uncertainty.
synthesis.inference: APRL should report failure warnings by evidence channel rather than one aggregate confidence number.

synthesis.title: Future state and geometry must be budgeted together
synthesis.facts: The batch ties WAM future state to mobile manipulation and sensor-specific 3D grounding.
synthesis.inference: A robot benchmark should cross future-cache age, sensor cue, and action success under the same rollout.

frontier_memory.label: Strengthening
frontier_memory.history: August 5 framed state validity as the weekly axis.
frontier_memory.body: August 6 makes the state-validity question evidence-channel specific.

frontier_memory.label: New signal
frontier_memory.history: Earlier WAM notes emphasized future prediction quality.
frontier_memory.body: Faster-WAM and DreamWAM shift the useful variable toward budgeted future-state representations.

frontier_memory.label: Missing axis
frontier_memory.history: Late July geometry checks emphasized SLAM and maps.
frontier_memory.body: Talk2Sensors adds sensor-cue agreement as a grounding validity axis.

strategy.title: Evidence-channel VLA audit harness
strategy.thesis: Cross instruction masking, visual distractors, future-state cache age, sensor cue removal, and risk-probe calibration in one robot rollout suite.
strategy.one_week: Instrument one VLA task with language-masked, visual-distractor, and future-cache ablations plus SAFECAST-style risk labels.
strategy.four_week: Build a reusable evidence-channel benchmark covering tabletop manipulation and one multi-sensor navigation scenario.
strategy.success: At least two evidence-channel perturbations predict distinct failure families before final action failure.
strategy.stop: Channel-specific probes collapse to the same signal as generic confidence or do not predict recovery choices.
strategy.asset: Evidence-channel perturbation logs, calibrated risk labels, and replayable sensor-cue ablation videos.

strategy.title: Sensor-cue grounding protocol
strategy.thesis: Evaluate whether language grounding uses texture, 3D geometry, radar velocity, or calibration evidence under explicit sensor dropout.
strategy.one_week: Create a small annotation sheet that labels every referred object by observable sensor cue and expected failure under cue removal.
strategy.four_week: Run camera-only, LiDAR-only, radar-only, and fused grounding on outdoor or campus robot scenes with controlled occlusion.
strategy.success: Grounding errors map to the removed cue rather than random box drift.
strategy.stop: Sensor-cue labels do not explain grounding failures beyond ordinary detection confidence.
strategy.asset: Cue-source annotation schema plus sensor-dropout grounding benchmark.
